page: Microsoft Azure D48ds_v6 is a general purpose virtual machine instance running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by dedicated x86_64 Intel Xeon 8573C processors operating at 4.2 GHz. The hardware configuration provides 48 vCPUs across 24 physical cores with 2 threads per core, supported by a 260 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. It includes 192.0 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per core. The instance is equipped with 2832 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and carries no dedicated GPUs.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong computational and memory performance across varied evaluations. The instance achieved top 25% results in Geekbench single-core (2140.0) and multi-core (19924.0) tests, as well as PassMark CPU score (62410.33) and database operations (25573.3). Advanced matrix and vector instruction support—including AMX-TILE, AMX-INT8, AVX-512, and AVX-VNNI—underpins strong CPU-based inference, showing top 10% performance in Geekbench image processing (20232.0) and LLM text generation for small 135M models (342.39 tokens/sec). Large-block uncached memory read bandwidth reached 232.42 GB/sec, while write bandwidth registered at 100.8 GB/sec.

The inclusion of 2832 GB of local NVMe SSD storage enhances efficiency for IO-intensive operations without requiring immediate network storage overhead. High-throughput benchmarks such as Redis SET operations (67.91 million ops/sec) and static web serving (80.58 GB/sec) highlight strong density per core. However, stress-ng CPU metrics and PassMark memory scores sit within the middle 50% range, indicating that raw synthetic integer throughput is consistent with mid-tier enterprise averages rather than specialized compute-optimized hardware.

Microsoft Azure D48ds_v6 is suited for large database workloads, high-throughput in-memory caching systems, CI/CD compilation pipelines, and CPU-driven machine learning inference tasks that benefit from advanced vector instructions and local NVMe storage.
